transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Gabe Rios (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Argent - Head of Platform), Marcus Yeo (Argent - Security Engineer), Priya Singh (Argent - PM)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you carving out time. we're going to walk through our data retention and redaction controls — quick intro then Gabe will show the console and API toggles.

[00:18] Laura Chen: Thanks Maya. We're mostly focused on how long you keep request logs and what we can turn off, and how PII is handled. We also need to understand KMS integration and deletion workflows.

[00:30] Maya Patel: Totally. Quick logistics — this is hosted demo, we'll touch on Dedicated and Private options later. Gabe, take it away?

[00:38] Gabe Rios: Sure, hi all. I'm Gabe, security and infra at Redwood. I'll start with a quick slide — bear with the auto captions, they're a bit off sometimes — then jump into the Console.

[00:50] Gabe Rios: So core controls we offer: request-level store/no-store toggle, automatic PII detection with redaction layers, configurable retention windows, audit logs with export, and customer KMS integration for at-rest encryption. On Dedicated/private we provide customer-managed KMS and optional air-gapped on-prem bundles.

[01:10] Marcus Yeo: When you say PII detection, is that pre- or post-processing? We need assurance it doesn't leave the system unredacted in logs.

[01:18] Gabe Rios: Good q. We do detection at ingestion — so the platform can flag and redact before it hits persistent logs. There are two layers: live request masking at the API edge and post-processing for any generated artifacts. We also support custom redact rules if you have company-specific patterns.

[01:33] Priya Singh: Is the PII model trainable? We have internal customer IDs that are not typical SSNs etc.

[01:39] Gabe Rios: You can add custom regexes or upload rule sets. We can also do a short evaluation where we match your sample data to see coverage. Important to note: the redact step can be tuned to either mask tokens in-place or remove entire fields when you enable structured output.

[01:55] Laura Chen: And the store/no-store toggle: is it per-API key, per-route, or global?

[02:02] Gabe Rios: We support multi-granular toggles: global account default, per-route policy, and even per-request override by header. So you could default to store for dev apps but set production keys to no-store.

[02:18] Maya Patel: Also worth calling out that no-store prevents storage of full request/response payloads in our long-term logs, but short-term ephemeral traces for debugging are available for a limited window and can be disabled entirely with higher plans or private deployments.

[02:36] Marcus Yeo: How short is short-term? We need to comply with our 24 hour SLA to not keep PII longer than a day for some customers.

[02:44] Gabe Rios: Default ephemeral trace retention is 7 days, but you can configure it down to 24 hours on our Dedicated plan, and in Private you control retention completely. We also have a feature to auto-purge traces older than X days and ability to purge by request id.

[03:01] Priya Singh: If we request deletion for a specific user record, how do you guarantee it's removed from all backups and logs?

[03:08] Gabe Rios: We have a deletion workflow: when a delete request is submitted we run a targeted purge across active indices and long-term storage. For backups, we mark the data as deleted and in dedicated/private setups we can wipe underlying volumes per policy; for hosted, backups are on a rolling retention, but we can provide proof of deletion via audit logs and timestamped deletion receipts. We also provide a compliance API to programmatically request deletion.

[03:34] Marcus Yeo: That deletion receipt — is it machine verifiable? We require cryptographic proof for a subset of regs.

[03:40] Gabe Rios: We can emit signed deletion receipts, and if you enable customer KMS we sign using your key material for higher assurance.

[03:50] Maya Patel: jumping into the console, you'll see on the left nav there's Data Controls -> Retention & Redaction. (screen share)

[04:02] [04:02] Gabe Rios: Ok, here's the route-level policy editor. Top: toggle store/ no-store, below: retention window in days, ephem traces toggle, and custom redact rules. I'll flip the store toggle to demonstrate.

[04:18] Gabe Rios: Note: when you set no-store, requests are still processed in-memory for inference but not written to long-term log stores, however metadata for billing (token counts) can still be kept unless you opt-out — we show that here as a separate billing telemetry toggle.

[04:34] Laura Chen: Billing telemetry...we need to keep cost attribution but don't want PII in billing. How does that work?

[04:40] Gabe Rios: Billing telemetry is aggregated counts and hashed identifiers. You can redact PII fields from telemetry and keep usage numbers intact. If you require zero telemetry, you can disable billing metadata but note that affects usage reporting.

[04:58] Marcus Yeo: On encryption: does Redwood hold keys or can we bring our own?

[05:03] Gabe Rios: Both. Hosted: we can manage keys, or you can supply a customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or Azure Key Vault). For Dedicated and Private you can require all keys be customer-managed and even HSM-backed if needed.

[05:18] Priya Singh: Are audit logs tamper-evident? We need immutability guarantees for forensics.

[05:24] Gabe Rios: Audit logs are append-only and we provide a checksum chain; for high-assurance setups we can ship logs to your S3 with write-once policies or to your SIEM via secure forwarding.

[05:36] [05:36] Laura Chen: Any SOC 2/ISO attestations we can review?

[05:40] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll share our SOC 2 Type II and ISO docs — Gabe will drop the attestation links after the call.

[05:48] Marcus Yeo: Can you run a quick API example for a no-store request? We want to see headers and how to include our tenant id without leaking it.

[05:55] Gabe Rios: Absolutely. Example curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "X-Redwood-Store: no-store" -H "X-Company-Tenant: <hashed-id>" -d '{"input":"..."}'  — note you can send hashed tenant ids and still get per-tenant accounting.

[06:18] Priya Singh: If we hash tenant id client-side, can you still do rollups by customer?

[06:22] Gabe Rios: Yes, as long as the hashing key is consistent per tenant. We also support deterministic tokenization for analytics without PII leakage.

[06:34] Maya Patel: Quick aside: some of the auto captions may show "Sample" instead of SAML — apologies. We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning.

[06:45] Laura Chen: For Private deployment how much network control do we get? We need VPC peering and private endpoints.

[06:51] Gabe Rios: Full control: VPC peering or Transit Gateway, private endpoints, and you can run the control plane in your region. We also support on-prem appliance for air-gapped environments.

[07:05] Marcus Yeo: Performance wise, does enabling redaction add latency? Our SLAs are tight.

[07:11] Gabe Rios: Minimal. Edge masking is optimized and runs inline — typical overhead is sub-10ms for simple regex rules; the PII model inference cost is a bit higher but we batch detection across requests. On Dedicated with GPU inference we can offload heavy detection, keeping tail latency low. We can run perf tests with your workload to quantify.

[07:34] Priya Singh: Do you offer an SDK to toggle store/no-store from the client side?

[07:38] Gabe Rios: Yes, our SDKs include flag helpers; for server-to-server calls you'd set the header. For browser flows you can use token-scoped keys with default no-store.

[07:50] Laura Chen: Can logs be forwarded to our SIEM in near real-time?

[07:54] Gabe Rios: Yes — we support log forwarding via secure streaming to Splunk, Datadog, and custom HTTPS sinks with mTLS.

[08:02] Maya Patel: I'll show the Optimize console briefly — this is where we give recommendations for batching and quantization that lower cost without affecting redaction behavior.

[08:12] [08:12] Gabe Rios: Note: optimizations are orthogonal to data handling — they change runtime but not retention rules.

[08:22] Priya Singh: About retention windows — can they be different per customer class? e.g., EU customers 30 days, US customers 90?

[08:28] Gabe Rios: Yes, we support policy trees by region, route, and customer tag. You can create policies that apply per tenant, and we can enforce region-specific storage (data residency) for EU tenants.

[08:42] Marcus Yeo: For legal holds, can we freeze deletion for certain records?

[08:47] Gabe Rios: We support legal hold flags that prevent purge. Those are tracked in audit logs and require an override workflow with elevated RBAC.

[08:58] Laura Chen: About the redaction model — does it ever alter model outputs if you remove fields? For structured outputs we might rely on certain keys.

[09:06] Gabe Rios: Good point. We provide structured output redaction where we remove or mask fields but preserve schema by returning placeholder tokens, so downstream parsing still works. You can choose mask or remove.

[09:18] Priya Singh: Is there a demo of the compliance API?

[09:21] Gabe Rios: Yes, we have a compliance endpoints doc. (link dropped in chat: https://redwood.ai/docs/data-retention) — I'll paste afterwards. It includes endpoints for delete request, audit log retrieval, and signed deletion receipts.

[09:35] Maya Patel: Quick live demo: I'll trigger a synthetic request with PII and show the redact event in audit log.

[09:42] [09:42] Gabe Rios: Sending example input: "Customer name: John Doe, SSN: 123-45-6789, account_number: 555-123"

[09:55] [09:55] Gabe Rios: The redact event shows: detected SSN -> masked as ***-**-**** in logs; the live response shows masked version depending on mask rules. The audit log shows detection confidence and rule id.

[10:12] Marcus Yeo: I notice the transcription spelled SSN weird on the slide — but seeing it live is helpful.

[10:17] Priya Singh: Can redact rules reference our internal PII table?

[10:21] Gabe Rios: You can upload lists or integrate with our rule API that pulls from your secure S3 or endpoints. We also support hashed lookups to avoid sharing raw values.

[10:34] Laura Chen: For the sample run we want the logs to show the deletion timeline and the signed deletion receipt.

[10:40] Gabe Rios: We'll run the sample and capture the deletion flow in the compliance API.

[10:46] [10:46] Maya Patel: A couple of common Qs — does retention affect model training/opt-in? We don't use customer prompts to train public models without opt-in; for hosted we have opt-out settings and explicit agreements.

[11:02] Marcus Yeo: So you have a contractual clause? We want to ensure data never used for training.

[11:07] Maya Patel: Yes, enterprise contracts can include clauses to prevent any training on customer data. For Dedicated/Private, data never leaves customer control unless explicitly allowed.

[11:20] Priya Singh: About incident response — if there's a suspected leakage, what's the process?

[11:24] Gabe Rios: We have an IR playbook, 24/7 incident response for enterprise customers, and we provide timely notifications, forensics and remediation steps. We'll share an incident response summary doc.

[11:36] Laura Chen: Marcus — any other security nitty-gritty?

[11:39] Marcus Yeo: Two more: SIEM integration for raw logs, and whether the audit logs include request bodies when store=no-store.

[11:48] Gabe Rios: Audit logs will never include full bodies if store=no-store unless you opt-in for specific debug traces. By default they include metadata, detection flags, and hash pointers. For SIEM we can forward events without payloads.

[12:02] Priya Singh: What about role-based access to purge endpoints? We need separation of duties.

[12:07] Gabe Rios: RBAC integrates with SSO (SAML) and you can require dual-approval for deletion operations. Role policies are configurable in the Console.

[12:21] Maya Patel: Demo: I'll go to the policy templates and show a per-tenant rule set.

[12:28] [12:28] Gabe Rios: Template library has GDPR, CCPA, PCI-ish starter templates so you can pick one and customize.

[12:36] Laura Chen: Any edge cases where redact could accidentally remove non-PII text? False positives?

[12:41] Gabe Rios: There can be false positives with regex-heavy rules; we recommend hybrid approach: model detection + allowlist for terms. We provide a review queue for flagged redactions so you can audit and whitelist.

[12:56] Priya Singh: Can we run a pilot with 100k requests to measure cost and latency?

[13:01] Gabe Rios: Yep — we do pilot benchmarks. We'll schedule a run and measure latency p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens. We'll also run with redaction enabled to measure overhead.

[13:12] Laura Chen: For billing, do you provide a breakdown of cost per route? We need chargeback.

[13:17] Maya Patel: Console shows per-route token breakdown and per-api-key costs — downloadable CSVs for finance.

[13:28] Marcus Yeo: If we go private, what's the timeline for deployment?

[13:33] Gabe Rios: Typical private deployment timeline is 6-10 weeks depending on environment and compliance work; Dedicated is 2-4 weeks. We'll refine in the pilot phase.

[13:45] Priya Singh: Anything in the roadmap for more granular PII categories?

[13:48] Gabe Rios: We're expanding categories and supporting custom taxonomy — should be available next quarter.

[13:57] [13:57] Maya Patel: Ok quick recap: we showed store/no-store, per-route toggles, PII detection and custom rules, retention windows, KMS options, audit logs and deletion receipts, SIEM forwarding, RBAC and SSO integration, and private/dedicated options.

[14:18] Laura Chen: That was really helpful. We'll need SOC2 docs and the KMS integration guide. Also send pricing for Dedicated and retention SLAs.

[14:28] Maya Patel: Will do. Gabe — toss the links and docs in the CRM and drop in chat.

[14:33] Gabe Rios: Will do. Links I'll share: SOC2/ISO pdf, KMS integration guide, compliance API reference, sample curl of no-store header, pilot run template.

[14:44] Marcus Yeo: One last question — do you provide hashed request ids for traceability without exposing PII?

[14:49] Gabe Rios: Yes, deterministic hashed request ids are supported and we'll show how to generate them securely.

[14:57] Priya Singh: Next steps from our side: provide a sample anonymized dataset and confirm pilot scope.

[15:03] Maya Patel: Great — we'll schedule the pilot run and share docs. Thanks everyone.

[15:09] Laura Chen: Thanks, bye.

[15:10] End of recording.
